core_obligations: Define c(Z -> X, N) by the equation i_* o j^* o C = p^* o c, verifying that both sides are bivariant classes and that p^* is bijective on Chow groups (proof lines 11926-11934).
Reduce the base change statement to the equality c' cap alpha' = c cap alpha' for alpha' in CH_k(X') (proof lines 11936-11944).

Compare the two constructions of the class attached to alpha' through the commutative diagram of the W's and the induced closed immersions, using independence of C under pushforward and the behaviour of flat pullback with proper pushforward (proof lines 11946-11991).
proof_roadmap: Well definedness of the class from the displayed equation (proof lines 11926-11934).
Reduction of base change compatibility to a cap-product identity (proof lines 11936-11944).
The commutative diagram and the induced closed immersions (proof lines 11946-11958).
Comparison of the two classes via independence and pullback-pushforward (proof lines 11960-11991).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the construction of the surrounding section defines a bivariant class c(Z -> X, N) in the completion A^*(Z -> X)^wedge, that this construction is compatible with base change as in Lemma labelled lemma-pullback-virtual-normal-sheaf, and that c lies in A^r(Z -> X) when N has constant rank r (statement lines 11911-11924). The proof defines the class by the displayed equation i_* o j^* o C = p^* o c(Z -> X, N), which is legitimate because both i_* o j^* o C and p^* are bivariant classes by Lemmas labelled lemma-flat-pullback-bivariant and lemma-push-proper-bivariant and because p^* is bijective on Chow groups by Lemma labelled lemma-vectorbundle (proof lines 11926-11934). For compatibility with base change it writes c and c' for the two classes, reduces by a formal argument to checking c' cap alpha' = c cap alpha' for alpha' in CH_k(X'), and compares the two computations of the class attached to alpha': the commutative diagram of W's, W_infinity's and normal cones induces closed immersions W' -> W x_{P^1_X} P^1_{X'}, W'_infinity -> W_infinity x_X X' and C_{Z'} X' -> C_Z X x_Z Z', and Lemma labelled lemma-gysin-at-infty-independent plus Lemma labelled lemma-flat-pullback-proper-pushforward show that the classes obtained from the two morphisms agree after pushforward and pullback along C_{Z'} X' -> N' (proof lines 11936-11991). Seeing that the defining equation determines a class and that the diagram comparison reduces the base change statement to a pushforward identity is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2; the reduction step is called formal by the author and is recorded verbatim in the editorial notes.
